FZUS52 KKEY 191515
CWFKEY

Coastal Waters Forecast for the Florida Keys
National Weather Service Key West FL
1015 AM EST Thu Nov 19 2026

Florida Bay, Hawk Channel and Straits of Florida from Ocean Reef
to south of Dry Tortugas, and the extreme southeastern Gulf of
America, including The Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary

Seas are given as significant wave height, which is the average
height of the highest 1/3 of the waves. Individual waves may be
more than twice the significant wave height.

The Wave Detail section highlights the period and direction of
origin for the highest-energy waves, as well as any long-period
swells moving in a different direction than the wind.

GMZ005-200315-
Synopsis for Keys coastal waters from Ocean Reef to Dry Tortugas
1015 AM EST Thu Nov 19 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
A developing area of low pressure off the East Coast of Florida 
will move northward this afternoon. While this low strengthens, 
it may tighten the gradient just enough for Friday through 
Saturday to result in another brief wind surge, especially off the
Upper Keys. Winds will also clock around to the west to 
northwest. The Keys will remain in overall weak flow with mainly 
light to potentially gentle breezes as we head into early next 
week.

The Approximate Shoreward Edge of the Gulf Stream as of November 
16, 2026...

12 NM south of Dry Tortugas Light, on Loggerhead Key
24 NM south of Cosgrove Shoal Light, off the Marquesas Keys
16 NM south of Sand Key Light, off Key West
 6 NM south of Looe Key, off Big Pine Key
 3 NM southeast of Sombrero Key Light, off Marathon
 1 NM southeast of Alligator Reef Light, off Islamorada 
 1 NM southeast of Molasses Reef Light, off Key Largo 
 1 NM southeast of Carysfort Reef Light, off Ocean Reef

Gulf Stream Information Courtesy of the Naval Oceanographic Office
and the National Weather Service in Key West, using data from 
RTOFS and NASA SPoRT sea surface temperatures.
